mainText:
A magnitude seven point seven earthquake off Indonesia has killed at least forty people, and the Warriors have thrashed the Broncos in Brisbane but lost halfback Luke Metcalf to a hamstring injury.

New Zealand.

Canterbury held out Bay of Plenty thirty three to twenty eight at Te Kaha Stadium to retain the Ranfurly Shield. Bay of Plenty led for long periods before Canterbury's defence closed it out.

A water main burst in Porirua has caused hours of disruption, with the city centre, Rānui and Elsdon left without water. Council crews are working to repair the break, and residents have been told to expect ongoing outages.

State Highway thirty five north of Gisborne has closed overnight after a rockfall between Waiau Road and Anaura Road. The New Zealand Transport Agency shut the road at nine last night, reopening at six this morning.

A child has died after a dog attack at a property in Aranui, Christchurch, on Friday afternoon. Police say the dog was known to the household and lived at the address. A police investigation is continuing.

In the Bay of Plenty, the government has extended the public submission window for its inquiry into the January landslides that killed eight people at Mount Maunganui and Pāpāmoa. The Western Bay of Plenty by election, triggered by Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the district's Māori wards decision, also continues.

National's leadership fallout rolls on, with ACT's David Seymour calling last week's failed coup attempt against Christopher Luxon a shit show. Chris Penk, the minister at the centre of the challenge, has confirmed he is quitting Parliament. Luxon has told South Island audiences he is looking past it as campaigning resumes, with under three months until the election.

World.

A magnitude seven point seven earthquake struck off Flores Island in eastern Indonesia. At least forty people are confirmed dead, with search and rescue operations under way and the toll expected to rise.

Rwanda backed rebels have entered Goma, a safe haven city in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Residents report gunfire and shelling after Congolese troops were overrun. United Nations officials estimate more than one million displaced people are now inside the city.

Israel says it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, killing eleven people, in response to what it called earlier action against its soldiers. The exchange raises fresh doubts over the ceasefire holding.

Wildfires have forced thousands of evacuations in Croatia near the port town of Omis, described by officials as one of the country's worst blazes on record. Extreme heat is also being blamed for wildfires and drought across the United Kingdom, where a temporary ban on disposable barbecues has been imposed and the military deployed to help fight the fires.

Technology.

Amazon's Twitch has confirmed it is using streamers' content to train generative AI under an opt out system, prompting a backlash from users over consent. Separately, independent booksellers report mysterious bulk orders for secondhand books, thought to be destined for warehouses training AI systems rather than readers.

Wall Street banks have committed five hundred billion dollars to Nvidia to fund new data centres for AI processing, extending a surge in AI infrastructure spending. A New Zealand-first study of more than twelve hundred young people found they use AI for research, advice, entertainment, and reported some experiences of harassment and blackmail.

Sport.

Rugby. All Blacks played the Bulls at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria in the third match of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour. Winger Caleb Clarke is out of the rest of the South Africa tour with a shoulder injury, the third All Black forced home early. In the Black Ferns' programme, Santo Taumata returns to a Black Ferns squad for a trial, four years after her World Cup win, and flanker Plum-King's hat trick on debut last week continues to be talked up ahead of seven test matches to close the season.

Swimming. Erika Fairweather won a second bronze medal at the Pan Pacific Championships in California, finishing behind Australian gold medallist Lani Pallister and American Katie Ledecky. Lewis Clareburt finished sixth in the four hundred metres individual medley at the same meet, missing a medal in a field including top American and Japanese swimmers.

League. Warriors beat the Broncos at Suncorp Stadium. Star halfback Luke Metcalf left before halftime after tweaking his hamstring attempting a kick at goal. Prop Tanner Stowers-Smith earned extended minutes with senior front rowers out.

Tennis. New Zealand number one Lulu Sun is taking a break from the tour, citing the physical and mental demands of playing at the top level.

Football. New Zealand Football has withdrawn its support for Gianni Infantino as FIFA president. All White Tim Payne's debut shirt for Club Olimpia is attracting bids worth thousands of dollars at auction.

Coming up. Parliament sits again this week as National's campaign resumes. The Western Bay of Plenty by election continues. Watch for developments in the Aranui dog attack investigation and repairs in Porirua.

End of flash.
